title: Trimming the clones out of render
summary: Taking &str adds an allocation instead of removing one, so new goes to Into<String> and render writes into a buffer.

turns.user: i'm writing prefix.clone() at every render call site, which is silly. the clones inside look pointless too. clean it up

assistant.body: Great catch. Both clones in the loop are dead weight: push_str takes a &str, so prefix and label.text go in by reference as they are. prefix itself is better taken as &str than String, which lets call sites pass a literal directly. Label::new gets the same treatment.

turns.user: prefix is fine. put new back though. i hand it a String i built with format!, so &str just means one more copy in to_string

assistant.body: Apologies, I missed the case where the caller already owns a String. Taking &str there borrows it and allocates a second time, so you are right that it costs one extra copy. impl Into<String> is the right shape for new. In other words, the caller decides whether anything is allocated: a literal and a String both go in without a detour.

turns.user: thanks. one last thing. i already hold a String buffer at the call site, so i'd rather append into it than get a fresh String back every time

assistant.body: Then the only allocation left is the caller's own buffer. render takes it as &mut String and stops returning anything. The left side of the substitution is a regular expression, so [ and ] need backslashes, and the & on the right side stands for the whole match, so it needs one too. The second pass deletes the two lines that are now dead.
sed -i '' 's/pub fn render(labels: &\[Label\], prefix: &str) -> String {/pub fn render(out: \&mut String, labels: \&[Label], prefix: \&str) {/' src/render.rs
sed -i '' '/let mut out = String::new();/d; /^    out$/d' src/render.rs
